title: Introduce RBACv2 policy-slab store, KMS path-proofing, and audit sample allocator
author: Sara Villar
release_notes: Adds a compact RBACv2 policy slab store, KMS path-proofing for residency-sensitive keys, and a lightweight audit sampling allocator to reduce ingestion costs while preserving forensic traceability.
description: Motivation: reduce policy decision latency and audit ingestion cost for high-cardinality tenants while preserving tamper-evident proofs and regional residency constraints. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) a compact "policy-slab" on-disk store that packs RBACv2 templates and derived role instances for fast lookups and incremental diffs; 2) a KMS path-proofing adapter that embeds a lightweight keyed proof into outbound KMS calls so downstream key-usage records can be correlated with RBAC slab snapshots for post-hoc residency verification; 3) an audit sample allocator that applies configurable deterministic sampling at the API gateway to keep high-cardinality operational telemetry within budget while maintaining representative forensic windows. Implementation summary: the policy-slab is implemented as a new service under internal/policy/slab with Go bindings and a minimal protobuf format; decision code paths were extended to consult slab indices before the general policy compiler fallback; the KMS adapter adds a signed "slab-hash" header and records a compact proof to the audit envelope; the sample allocator lives at edge/apigw and supports tenant, route, and sensitivity tiers with deterministic sampling seeds. Checklist: - [x] design doc and architecture diagram (linked in PR) - [x] unit and integration tests for slab store, decision fallback, and sample allocator - [x] end-to-end KMS instrumentation tests verifying slab-hash propagation - [x] compatibility shim for older policy formats in policy-compiler - [x] performance bench: median decision latency improvement ~18% on synthetic policy mix Rollout plan: start with canary in us-east-1 for 48h with sampling defaults conservative (10% for high-cardinality tenants), enable slab read-only mode for 2 weeks, then enable slab write for rollout, and finally enable KMS path-proof header in a staged manner. Security considerations: slab store is persisted to the same encrypted store used by policy-compiler and access gated by operator-scoped RBAC; proofs are HMAC-signed with a rotating key stored in KMS; audit samples keep full envelopes for sampled requests and compressed hashes for non-sampled requests to limit PII exposure. Backwards compatibility: older agents and SDKs ignore the slab-hash header; policy compiler will fall back to existing enabled behavior if slab lookup fails. Follow-ups: 1) add console UI to inspect slab snapshots and per-tenant sampling rate history (ENG-1452) 2) integrate with Optimize to recommend sampling rates based on cost/quality (ENG-1503) 3) implement multi-region slab replication with causal consistency (ENG-1620).
